existing_overlap: No staged article defines inference itself. Adjacent articles are linked and differentiated: ai-term-test-time-compute (extra compute spent during inference), ai-reasoning-models-explained (reasoning vs inference wording), ai-term-quantization and ai-term-prompt-caching (named as cost levers, not explained). The one-line definition in ai-glossary-50-terms (live article) was not re-read.
notes: Counted with app.guides.pack_ingest._body_length on the final pack.json (paragraphs, rich_paragraph text including the five article-link labels = 86 characters, list items, table cells, callout title and text; headings, captions and sources excluded): 2499. Without link labels: 2413. Source conflicts with the brief, source wins: (1) brief and catalogue say inference = 推論 and reasoning = 推理 as if settled, but Taiwan's NAER terminology database (terms.naer.edu.tw) renders inference as 推理 in the computer-science glossary (電子計算機名詞) and as 推論 in statistics, with several glossaries listing both; the article therefore states the series convention as an editorial choice and not a dictionary rule. (2) batch brief says the character count excludes link text yet also says it follows _body_length, which includes rich_paragraph link labels; the figure above is the tool's. Illustrative scenario (two question types for a fictional guesthouse assistant) is original and labelled unmeasured; no vendor prices, speeds, model names or paper throughput multipliers appear. Diagram carries no numbers other than the drawing year 2026 (present in the table caption). Dry-run ingest passes; only the no_summary warning that the sandbox example also raises.
